account:
Today has seemed quiet and routine, with no confirmed unusual trouble. During the morning market walk I heard several townsfolk say the baker had been carrying a sack of wheat at the bakery. That sounds consistent with baking supplies; I have no evidence of another purpose. My tea host also said the baker was busy preparing fresh loaves for today's market and reported no pressing neighbourhood concerns.

There was some confusion about the tea appointment: the secretary could not initially identify the host or confirm the address despite asking near the docks and warehouse. I found the neighbour at the east-bank cottage near (16, -60, 105), arrived for three o'clock tea, and was invited again tomorrow. I still do not know the host by any name other than neighbour. I gave the secretary the location to clarify the appointment.

The secretary reported no new correspondence and returned the appointment book to its chest. Tomorrow's ten o'clock appointment is a grain inspection at the mill. I requested existing stock and delivery records and information about shortages or storage concerns, without moving supplies. The secretary went to confirm the inspection and intends to report at eight tomorrow if unable to catch me this evening. This is preparation for scheduled town business, not evidence that a shortage exists.

I have now returned home for the nineteen o'clock appointment. Tomorrow I should attend the office at eight, read the appointment book, and hear the secretary's confirmation before visiting the mill.
